# Jag Outer Banks Properties

> Outer Banks vacation rentals and local attraction guides, covering Corolla to
> Nags Head, North Carolina.

Jag Outer Banks Properties rents a small, hand-picked set of vacation properties on the Outer Banks
and publishes guides to the attractions near them. Guides are written from local
knowledge and checked against official sources.

## Properties

- [Browse all properties](https://jagobxproperties.com/): current vacation rentals with full photo
  galleries and direct booking links.

## Guides

- [The Corolla Wild Horses: Fifty Feet Is the Law, Not a Suggestion](https://jagobxproperties.com/articles/corolla-wild-horses/): Where the Corolla wild horses actually live, how to get up the beach to see them, and the Currituck County rules that carry real penalties.
- [The Elizabethan Gardens: Closed Every January, and Nobody Tells You](https://jagobxproperties.com/articles/elizabethan-gardens/): Ten acres of formal garden next door to Fort Raleigh, with Renaissance Italian statuary, $12 admission, $5 dogs, and a January closure that catches people out.
- [Fort Raleigh: The Free One Everybody Drives Past](https://jagobxproperties.com/articles/fort-raleigh/): A free national historic site on Roanoke Island with the Lost Colony earthworks, two walking trails and a visitor center open 9 to 5 every day.
- [Nags Head Woods: Sixteen Parking Spaces and a Mountain Forest](https://jagobxproperties.com/articles/nags-head-woods/): A free Nature Conservancy preserve in Kill Devil Hills with eight trails, 550 plant species and a car park that fills by mid morning.
- [Whalehead in Corolla: Tiffany Glass in a Duck Hunting Lodge](https://jagobxproperties.com/articles/whalehead-corolla/): A 1925 mansion with cork floors and signed Tiffany fixtures, on 39 soundfront acres in Corolla. $7 for adults, the park around it is free, and the museum keeps weekday hours.
- [Jennette's Pier: Two Dollars to Walk on the Ocean](https://jagobxproperties.com/articles/jennettes-pier/): A thousand feet of concrete pier in Nags Head. $2 to walk on, $15 to fish, open year round, and run by the state aquariums.
- [NC Aquarium on Roanoke Island: The Rainy Day Plan](https://jagobxproperties.com/articles/nc-aquarium-roanoke-island/): Timed tickets, a shark tank, otters and a working sea turtle hospital, twenty minutes inland in Manteo. What to know before you book.
- [Bodie Island Lighthouse: Climbing It, and What It Costs](https://jagobxproperties.com/articles/bodie-island-lighthouse/): 219 steps to the top of an 1872 tower on the Nags Head marsh. The 2026 climb season, ticket rules, the 42 inch height limit, and what is still closed.
- [Currituck Beach Lighthouse: Climbing the Corolla Tower](https://jagobxproperties.com/articles/currituck-beach-lighthouse/): 220 steps up an unpainted brick tower in Corolla, open March to November for $13. Season dates, the age rule, and why it beats Bodie Island.
- [Wright Brothers National Memorial: What to Know Before You Go](https://jagobxproperties.com/articles/wright-brothers-national-memorial/): The first powered flight happened on this field in Kill Devil Hills, and the ground still shows exactly where. Hours, the $10 fee, the four flight markers, and how long to allow.
- [Jockey's Ridge State Park: What to Know Before You Go](https://jagobxproperties.com/articles/jockeys-ridge-state-park/): Jockey's Ridge in Nags Head is the tallest natural sand dune on the East Coast, and it is free to visit. Hours, parking, sandboarding rules and the best time to climb.
